description:
## Goal

Preserve exact partial composite returns across direct callable edges without falsely claiming that the whole tuple exists as a runtime ValueRef. A child field with a ValueRef representation is not evidence that its parent composite has a ValueRef carrier.

## Failure and cause

On behavior/mailbox_closure_reduce, the Enum.reduce wrapper lambda returns a semantic two-tuple under exact demand TupleFields([Ignore, Whole]). The :cont field is intentionally absent and the accumulator field is live. The transport recipe produces shape tuple(nothing, lane(any)) but lifts the live child carrier to the outer tuple. Backend and native then correctly interpret the outer ValueRef as a whole-materialization obligation and attempt to read the absent :cont value.

This is carrier provenance, not missing runtime demand. Do not widen the ignored tag, add a fallback Whole demand, or weaken backend/native validation.

## Correct model

Composite structural lanes and the optional whole-composite carrier are independent. Direct partial transport carries the demanded fields as multiple values with outer carrier Absent. Only explicit whole-value observation, escape, or an opaque/first-class boundary requires a complete composite ValueRef. Joining inner field representations must not manufacture that parent obligation.

Elixir/OTP provides the guide: known-list Enum.reduce bypasses its tagged protocol wrapper and passes only the accumulator; generic Enumerable boundaries construct and pass a complete tagged tuple. Within local control flow, the Erlang Core optimizer replaces immediately destructured tuples with multiple values and reconstructs the term only if the whole value is referenced.

## Acceptance

1. Add a focused RED reproducing the exact wrapper return: TupleFields([Ignore, Whole]) yields tuple(nothing, live lane) with outer carrier Absent, and all three mailbox_closure_reduce doors pass.
2. Prove a live child ValueRef does not promote its parent tuple carrier on a direct-only path.
3. Prove explicit Whole and boxed/first-class consumers still require a complete outer ValueRef and all fields needed for safe materialization.
4. Preserve same-arity field reprojection and boxed-owner guarantees from fz-tfn.36.
5. Backend and native agree: neither reads an ignored field on a direct partial return, while both reject an actually incomplete whole-value materialization.
6. No widening, compatibility shim, aggregate authority, string identity, or new scan. Put carrier provenance at the data-model boundary that makes invalid states unrepresentable.
7. Run focused transport/runtime-demand/backend/native tests, mailbox fixture on all doors, full library, serial fixture matrix, formatting, check, strict clippy, and update agent/user docs where the carrier rule is described.
8. Ticket-scoped cold adversarial review before the single commit; close this ticket with that commit. Then resume fz-kdt.4.

## Data-model boundary

`TransportRecipe::Tuple` composes each child's exact structural shape unchanged and derives the parent carrier only from demand on the composite itself. `ShapeDemand::Whole` and a first-class callable obligation on the composite produce an outer `ValueRef`; a partial `TupleFields` demand produces `Absent` even when a retained child also has a `ValueRef` carrier. `TransportLayout` may expose structural lanes and an optional whole ref simultaneously, so a parent keeps the child's structural lanes and never promotes the child's optional carrier to itself. Public callable returns continue to set their explicit outer carrier at the public-return recipe boundary.
title: Keep direct partial tuple returns unboxed
